specAnchors.text: understand how stars can be classified according to their colour

primer.text: A star's colour is a thermometer: red stars are the coolest at around 3000 K and blue stars the hottest at around 30 000 K. Swelling stars cool and redden; shrinking stars heat up and whiten.

modules.title: Colour and temperature
modules.opening: Stars can be classified by colour, and colour tracks surface temperature: red stars are the coolest at roughly 3000 K, blue stars the hottest at roughly 30 000 K. Expanding astronomical objects cool while contracting ones heat up, so a star's colour shifts as its size changes.
keyPoints: Stars get classified by the colour of their light.
The colour of a star tracks its surface temperature.
Red stars run coolest — near 3000 K; blue stars run hottest, near 30 000 K.
Expanding astronomical objects cool; contracting ones heat up.
Red giants redden as they expand and cool; white dwarfs whiten as they contract and heat up.

low.restatement: Red = cool (≈3000 K), blue = hot (≈30 000 K) — colour is the thermometer.
low.analogy: Metal in a forge: it glows red first and turns blue-white only when hotter — stars follow the same rule.
low.examPointer: Flip the everyday intuition deliberately: write 'red = cool' at the top of the answer space.

medium.restatement: Temperature and size are linked: expansion cools a star redder, contraction heats it whiter — which is why late-stage colours differ.
medium.analogy: Spray vs kettle: a wide spray cools (redder), the compressed jet concentrates heat (whiter).
medium.examPointer: Link colour change to expansion or contraction explicitly — the causal chain carries the mark.

modules.title: Colour shifts in stellar evolution
modules.opening: Infrared flows from warm bodies; visible light joins in only once a body is extremely hot, so the colour a star emits depends on how hot it is. As a star's life advances this colour shifts: the swelling red giant cools and reddens, and the collapsing white dwarf heats and whitens.
keyPoints: The colour an object emits depends on how hot it is.
Warm bodies radiate infrared; only extremely hot ones add visible light.
Swelling into a red giant, the star reddens as its surface cools.
Contracting into a white dwarf, it heats up and whitens.

low.restatement: Hot objects emit visible light; cooler ones only infrared — so colour announces temperature.
low.analogy: An electric hob element: barely warm gives nothing you can see, hot gives red, white-hot means very hot indeed.
low.examPointer: Evolution questions often hide the colour cue — connect expansion-cooling to reddening and contraction-heating to whitening.

medium.restatement: The red giant reddens and the white dwarf whitens for one reason: surface temperature moves as size moves.
medium.analogy: A wave relaxing (spreading out, cooling) versus a wave squeezed into a narrow channel (concentrating, heating).
medium.examPointer: Name the temperature, then the colour — that order matches the mark scheme.

glossary.definition: The temperature a star's surface radiates at, shown directly by its colour.
A swollen, cooler, redder late stage of a star's life.
A contracted, hotter, whiter end stage that still glows faintly.
